findings.title: Materials' 57-point lens gap signals earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials trades at 16.54x forward but 34.77x trailing, a 57-point percentile gap — the widest in the table. The market is pricing a 110 percent earnings surge, which would be a historic reversal for a sector whose trailing multiple sits at the 83rd percentile.

findings.title: Utilities' forward optimism clashes with trailing floor
findings.body: Utilities' forward P/E sits at the 32nd percentile while its trailing multiple is at the 3rd — a 29-point gap. Analysts expect only 4 percent earnings growth, yet the forward lens is far richer, suggesting the market is paying up for stability rather than expansion.

findings.title: Information Technology's forward multiple hits zero
findings.body: Information Technology's forward P/E of 17.72 is at the 0th percentile of its five-year range, while its trailing multiple is at the 18th. The 63 percent implied earnings growth is the second-highest in the table, but the market is refusing to pay for it — a stark disconnect between estimates and price.
